detailed_rationale:
Capri Global Capital (CGCL) is a diversified NBFC lending across MSME finance, affordable housing finance, construction finance, car-loan distribution, and gold loans (launched August 2022, now a meaningful growth engine). As a financial-sector lender, its balance-sheet leverage is structural rather than a red flag, so the relevant lens is asset quality, margins and capital rather than D/E.

On that basis the business is executing well. Net profit has stepped up each of the last several quarters (~Rs.236cr to ~Rs.353cr), asset quality is improving (gross NPA ~1.40%, net NPA ~0.90% as of December 2025, trending favorably), net interest margin is a very healthy ~30%, and ROE on a current run-rate basis is around 16% -- notably better than the trailing ROE figure in the quant dataset (~9.3%), consistent with a business that is scaling out of an opex-heavy branch build-out phase (particularly the newer gold-loan vertical) into a higher-return steady state. Revenue growth has been strong (1y ~26%, 3y CAGR ~46%), though we would treat the 3-year figure with some caution since a chunk of it reflects the gold-loan business ramping from a very small base rather than fully steady-state growth. Promoter holding has drifted down modestly over three years, which typically reflects capital raises to fund AUM growth in a scaling NBFC rather than a governance concern by itself, though it is worth monitoring alongside future capital raises.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold and our research supports it -- genuinely improving asset quality, strong and improving margins, and credible diversified growth drivers (gold loans, affordable housing, MSME), but not yet a long enough steady-state track record post-diversification to justify treating this as a clear rescue-to-better-than-Hold case, nor any red flag that would warrant escalation.
summary: Capri Global is a fast-growing, diversified NBFC with lending books in MSME, affordable housing and gold loans, and its numbers are moving in the right direction: profits rising each quarter, asset quality improving, and margins strong. We rate it a Hold: the growth story is credible, but a meaningful share of recent growth comes from a newer, smaller gold-loan business scaling up, so we would want to see this sustain over more quarters before treating the pace as fully steady-state.
positive_para: The business is diversified across several structurally growing Indian lending categories -- MSME credit, affordable housing finance, and gold loans -- and the numbers show real operating momentum: net profit has risen every recent quarter, gross and net NPAs are both low and improving, and net interest margin is unusually strong at around 30%. Current run-rate ROE (~16%) is meaningfully better than the trailing figure in the scorecard, suggesting the newer verticals are moving past their initial branch-and-systems build-out cost drag into a more profitable steady state.
negative_para: A good portion of the impressive year-on-year growth is coming from the gold-loan business scaling up from a small base (launched only in August 2022), so the eye-catching growth rates should be read with some base-effect caution rather than extrapolated at face value into perpetuity. Promoter holding has declined modestly over three years, consistent with capital raises to fund growth but a trend worth tracking, and free cash flow remains structurally negative as is typical for a scaling lender -- meaning continued external capital (debt or equity) will likely be needed to sustain the current pace of AUM growth.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 19-26x earnings (scrape-date PE in the CSV is somewhat stale versus the more current ~19.4x we found) and about 3x book value, the market is pricing continued high-teens-to-20%+ growth with stable-to-improving asset quality. Given NIM is strong and NPAs are improving, this looks close to fair value for a diversified NBFC executing well, though the multiple leaves limited room for the gold-loan growth engine to disappoint or for a broader NBFC credit-cost cycle to turn.
